title: Source record
description: One cited source: its citation data, where to find it, its archived copies and history, and the rights to use it. Stored as content/sources/<first letter of key, or _other>/<key>.yaml.

key.description: Citation key used in text as [@key]. Must equal the file name.

kind.description: court-rule: rules of any court, including local rules. congressional-document: a document of Congress other than a statute: a committee hearing, a House or Senate report, a committee print, or a Congressional Research Service product; citation.genre names which, and legislative holds its Congress, committees, bills and the laws it is the history of. federal-agency-document: a federal agency's own published document other than a regulation or Federal Register notice, such as a National Indian Gaming Commission opinion, enforcement action or bulletin; citation.genre names which. intergovernmental-agreement: a compact or agreement between governments, such as a tribal-state gaming compact. journal: a periodical as a whole, cited as a place to search.

citation.description: Citation Style Language JSON item (https://docs.citationstyles.org/). Rendered into footnotes by citeproc. 'id' is filled from 'key' at build time.

original_link.description: Where the original is published, if online.

retrieved.description: Date the source was last consulted.

archives.description: Archived copies. At least one is expected for every web source.

file.description: A copy stored in the project's R2 bucket. Served publicly only when rights.redistribution is true.

storage_key.description: Object key of the stored copy in the project's R2 bucket.

checksum.description: SHA-256 hash of the stored file, in lowercase hexadecimal.

history.description: Changes to the web page or file at the source's address, from the Internet Archive and scheduled re-checks. Versions of the document itself (an amendment, a revised constitution, a new edition of a code) are recorded in content/documents/ instead, and the source names its version in document_version (decision record 0018).

document_version.description: When this source is one version of a document that changes over time (a compact, an amendment, a constitution, an edition of a code or court rules), the document history record and the version it is. The version names this source in turn; scripts/lint_records.py checks that the two agree (decision record 0018).

shares_link_with.description: Keys of other source records at the same address that are different documents, such as several statutes on one chapter page or a case that quotes a statute. Without it, two records at one address (ignoring the scheme, 'www.', a trailing slash or an index page) are treated as duplicates by scripts/lint_records.py.

citator.description: Negative-treatment check for cases and statutes (e.g. KeyCite).

courtlistener.description: The case as CourtListener (Free Law Project) files it, matched by citation, case name and year from CourtListener's quarterly bulk data by scripts/caselaw/check_case_citations.py. Later uses (links, the citation graph, parentheticals) start from the cluster number.

citation.description: The citation that matched, such as "436 U.S. 49".

case_name.description: The case name as CourtListener gives it.

release.description: Date of the bulk data release checked.

argument_timing.description: The argument's transcript with the moment each turn begins, for the argument player: one per day of argument with a recording. Where the Court has a transcript, its turns are timed against the recording; where it has none (before the October 1968 term, and four later arguments), the transcript is the words a speech recognition model heard, with the speakers not marked. Made and stored by scripts/caselaw/supreme_court_argument_timing.py.

made.description: Whether the text is the Court's transcript, timed, or our own made by speech recognition.

model.description: The speech recognition model that heard the recording ("Whisper small.en").

turns.description: Turns (or, for our own transcripts, paragraphs) in the file.

recording.description: The recording's files in playing order (the record's argument_audio files), each with its length as heard; the times are from the start of the first.

span.description: Where the argument lies in the recording, in seconds: all of it for a case's own file, part of a whole day's reels.

counsel.description: Who argued: from the transcript's appearances and headings, or, with no transcript, from the report's syllabus (research/supreme-court-coverage/argument-counsel.csv).

title.description: Office or city, as the appearances give it.

for.description: Whom the counsel argued for, as the source says it.

source.description: The report the counsel is named in, where there is no transcript.

sections.description: Where each counsel's argument (and rebuttal) begins, in seconds, from the transcript's headings.

argument_transcripts.description: Official transcripts of the court hearing the case argued, one per day of argument. For the Supreme Court, from the Court's own site, which has one for every argument since the October 1968 term (the Court's library scans before the 2000 term). Listed and stored by scripts/caselaw/supreme_court_argument_transcripts.py; the plan is research/supreme-court-coverage/argument-transcripts.csv.

date.description: The day of the argument, as the transcript's list dates it.

docket.description: The docket number the transcript is listed under.

source.description: Who publishes the transcript ("Supreme Court of the United States").

link.description: The transcript file at its source.

argument_audio.description: Sound recordings of the court hearing the case: each argument, and the court announcing its opinion where the recording holds that. For the Supreme Court, from the Court's own site (every argument since the October 2010 term) and the National Archives (Record Group 267, every recording since the 1955 term). Listed and stored by scripts/caselaw/supreme_court_argument_audio.py; the plan is research/supreme-court-coverage/argument-audio.csv.

date.description: The day the recording was made, as the source dates it.

source.description: Who holds the recording: the court itself ("Supreme Court of the United States", "United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit") or the "National Archives".

link.description: The recording file at its source.

catalog.description: The National Archives Catalog entry for the recording.

whole_session.description: The file holds the Court's whole session that day (one reel), so the case is somewhere inside it, with other cases.

note.description: Where the source's date differs from the case's argument or decision date.

duration_seconds.description: Length of the recording, read from the stored file.

held.description: True when the stored file is kept privately and not served (for example, a recording about a child).

court_dates.description: A case's dates other than its decision (citation.issued), each as the official report or the court's own record prints it: the U.S. Reports or the Court's own prints and docket for the Supreme Court, the reporter's head matter or the court's slip opinion for other courts. A date the source does not print is left out, never taken from secondary sources. The case box shows each date on its own line in order, with the decision among them (site/src/lib/server/case-facts.ts, pdf/pipeline/typst-writer.mjs). Checked by hand; the review is in research/reviews/2026-11-23-court-dates.csv.

argued.description: Oral argument, every day the source names.

argued_and_submitted.description: Argued and submitted for decision the same day, as the Ninth Circuit and others print it.

heard.description: Heard, as the First Circuit prints the day of argument.

submitted.description: Submitted for decision without argument, or on the briefs.

filed.description: Only when the opinion was filed on a different day from the decision, such as a district court opinion signed one day and filed the next.

printed.description: The dates exactly as the source prints them, to check against.

source.description: The official report, court print, docket or reporter head matter the dates come from.

note.description: Where other sources give a different date, and why this one is used.

caption.description: A case's caption as the official report prints it, naming the parties and their roles ("Samuel A. Worcester, Plaintiff in Error v. The State of Georgia"). Shown under Parties and nations on the case's page (site/src/lib/server/case-pages.ts). Letter case may be changed from small capitals; the words may not.

source.description: The official report or court print the caption comes from.

opinions.description: Each opinion in a case and the page of the official report where it starts, read from the report itself. The case's page lists them, each linked to its first page in the saved copy of the official report, and says which opinion each quotation comes from (site/src/lib/case-opinions.ts). Checked by hand.

source.description: The official report the pages come from.

enum: concurrence in part and in the judgment
concurrence in part and in the result
concurrence in part and dissent in part
concurrence in part, concurrence in the judgment in part, and dissent in part
concurrence in part, concurrence in the result in part, and dissent in part
concurrence in the judgment and dissent in part

justice.description: The writer, as the record's supreme_court.justices names them, or the judge's name for other courts. "The Court" for a per curiam opinion.

page.description: The report page where the opinion starts.

scan_page.description: The page of the saved scan that holds the opinion's first page, given only where counting from the case's first page would miss it (the scan has an inserted map or blank leaf before it).

note.description: Anything a reader should know, such as an opinion the report does not print in full.

case_box.description: The case's box: its summary, quotations and treatment, which every essay that places the case (":::: case <key>" and "::::" with nothing between) and the case's page show, and the print book prints (site/src/lib/essays/record-boxes.ts, pdf/pipeline/record-boxes.mjs; Trevor, Nov. 24, 2026). Each text is Markdown in the essay syntax and may cite sources as [@key, at 5]. Its reading, if any, follows the box as an Analysis block.

background.description: The law and events behind the case.

holding.description: What the court held. The case's preview shows it (site/src/lib/server/case-previews.ts).

quotes.description: The court's words, each cited to the case at its pinpoint.

treatment.description: How later courts treated the case. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line.

topics.description: The topics the index of cases by topic lists the case under, as shown: "Sovereign immunity" (site/src/lib/essays/case-topics.ts).

later_cases.description: The later cases that treated this one negatively, each by kind of treatment, shown under Treatment on the case's page, in the essays and in the print book (site/src/lib/essays/record-boxes.ts, pdf/pipeline/record-boxes.mjs). Written by scripts/caselaw/later_cases.py from the Negative Treatment list of a hand-pulled Westlaw print (Trevor, Nov. 27, 2026: name the cases rather than count them).

checked.description: The day the print was delivered.

source.description: The print's key in the private captures.

name.description: The case's name, shown in italics.

citation.description: The rest of its Indigo Book citation: "474 B.R. 687 (B.A.P. 8th Cir. 2012)".

case.description: The key of this project's record of the case (its page, /cases/<key>).

copy.description: The key of the opinion copy this site serves (/copies/view/<key>).

law_box.description: The law's box: what it does, quotations from it and how it was treated, which every essay that places the law (":::: law <key>" and "::::" with nothing between) shows and the print book prints (site/src/lib/essays/record-boxes.ts, pdf/pipeline/record-boxes.mjs). Each text is Markdown in the essay syntax and may cite sources as [@key, sec. 3].

quotes.description: The law's words, each cited to the law at its section.

treatment.description: Amendments, court readings, repeal. Paragraphs are separated by a blank line.

legislative.description: For a congressional-document: where in Congress it comes from and what it is about, from GovInfo's and Congress.gov's own data (scripts/law/congressional_documents.py, scripts/law/crs_reports.py). A law's page lists, under Legislative history, the documents that name it in laws.

chamber.description: The chamber whose document it is; congress for a joint committee's print or a Congressional Research Service product.

congress.description: The Congress, such as 100 for the 100th Congress (1987-1988).

committees.description: The committees and subcommittees that held the hearing or wrote the report, as GovInfo names them.

bills.description: The bills it is on, such as "S. 1234 (100th Cong.)".

laws.description: Keys of the federal statute records it is part of the legislative history of (a report on the bill that became the law), or, for a Congressional Research Service product, the laws Congress.gov relates it to.

held.description: The days a hearing was held.

govinfo_package.description: The document's package on GovInfo, such as CRPT-118srpt12 or SERIALSET-13736_00_00-009-0157-0000.

crs_status.description: For a Congressional Research Service product: whether Congress.gov lists it as current or archived.

state_law.description: For a state statute section found by a state's Indian law sweep (research/analyses/2026-11-26-state-statutes-pilot.md): how it bears on Native nations and how to cite it. Every relevant section gets a record, labeled core or incidental (Trevor, Nov. 26, 2026).

relevance.description: core: the section's subject is Native nations or Indian people, such as a tribal-state compact law or a state Indian child welfare act. incidental: the section is about something else but gives a nation, tribal government, tribal court, tribal member or Indian land a specific legal role, right, duty or exemption. Set by an AI reader and Unverified until a person checks it.

citation.description: The section's citation as the Indigo Book writes it, such as "Okla. Stat. tit. 10, § 40 (2026)".

act.description: The named act the section belongs to, when it has one, such as "Oklahoma Indian Child Welfare Act".

page.description: The page of the official title PDF where the section starts, when the official text is a PDF.

reading_links.description: Other places a reader can read this case or law, found and checked by scripts/caselaw/reading_links.py from the settings in research/reading-links/sites.yaml. The website shows them beside the citation.

access.description: official: the government's own text; free; subscription: needs an account, such as Westlaw or Lexis; background: not legal authority, such as Wikipedia.

unchecked.description: The site turns away automated checks, so the link follows the site's own stable address pattern without a check.

supreme_court.description: Who decided a Supreme Court case: the Court (named for the Chief Justice), the bench, the vote and each justice's part. From Oyez's public case data (scripts/law/supreme_court_benches.py), or from the official report where Oyez has none.

court.description: The Court named for its Chief Justice, such as "Warren Court".

natural_court.description: The bench that heard the case, as Oyez names it, such as "Warren Court (1958-1962)".

opinion.description: The opinion the justice wrote: majority, concurrence, dissent and the like.

source.description: The Oyez case, or the official report when Oyez has no vote data.

note.description: What the source does not settle, such as votes the report does not state.

contribution.description: For a source that reached the project from a person (an interview, a told story, a family document) rather than from publication: the public-safe summary of its contribution filing. Signed forms, recordings and contact details stay in the private filing (docs/contributions.md). When the contributor statement grants use, rights.status is 'granted' with basis 'permission'.

tribes.description: Tribe profile ids this source concerns.

nations_in_case.description: For a court case: each Native nation or people the case names, as a party or as what the case is about, matched to its nation record. 'tribes' lists the same nation ids. A name that does not match one nation today is listed under not_linked with the reason, rather than guessed.

checked.description: When the names were checked against the opinion.

named_as.description: The name the case gives, which may be a former name, an older spelling, a reservation or a historical nation.

role.description: party: the nation itself is a party (plaintiff, defendant, petitioner, respondent or intervenor). government: its officials, council, court, agency or business arm is a party. subject: the case concerns the nation, its land, its court or its members, but the nation is not a party.

historical.description: True when the case names a historical nation or band whose people are today part of the linked nation, or of several nations.

jurisdictions.description: The governments or legal orders the source concerns.

methods.description: Dispute resolution methods the source establishes, describes or analyzes. Add a method record with status 'proposed' for any process that has none.

topics.description: Free tags for grouping in bibliographies, e.g. history, treatise, court-connected-program, full-faith-and-credit. Not a fixed list.

subjects.description: The subjects of Indian law a case or law belongs to, from a closed list, so the legal history essay and the timeline can be read by subject (refactor and improvements report, Nov. 24, 2026, section 9.3, step 4). Dispute resolution stays one of them (Trevor, Nov. 24, 2026). Shown as: Land; Treaties; Jurisdiction; Criminal law; Family and children; Gaming; Environment and natural resources; Religion; Culture; Government; Citizenship and status; Taxation; Trust responsibility; Sovereign immunity; Tribal courts; Dispute resolution. Unlike `topics`, which are free tags, these are a fixed list.

annotation.description: Markdown. The annotated-bibliography entry: what the source is and why it matters to the project. Quotations carry pinpoints; the project's own judgments are labeled (project analysis).

access.description: How to reach the full text, so a researcher knows what needs a subscription database or a library.

open.description: True when the full text is free to read online.

note.description: What to pull and how, e.g. the annotated code section to open in Westlaw.

found_in.description: Research session ids (file names without .md) that found or updated this source.

review.description: For a record a script wrote: the cross-checks the script ran between independent sources and what each found (scripts/caselaw/supreme_court_native_cases.py). "verified" means every check agreed or was confirmed in the official report itself, not that a person has read the record; a person who reads it records that with status "reviewed". The record's other `checked` dates are the day the script read the sources.

by.description: The script, or the person who reviewed it.

result.description: agree: the sources agree. confirmed: they differ or one is missing, and the official report prints what the record says (the words it prints are in detail). settled: an AI reader read the scan, but the report's text has not confirmed the reading. differs, missing: unsettled.

boxReading.description: A short, neutral reading of the entry's place in the law. An essay that places the box shows it right after the box as an "Analysis" block (record-boxes.ts, readingMarkdown); the case's own page does not. It is the site's interpretation, not a statement of the sources. Readings written for the model code belong in its commentary, not here (Trevor, Nov. 24, 2026).

title.description: The Analysis block's title, naming what it reads: "*Worcester v. Georgia* (1832)" or "Indian Citizenship Act (1924)".

text.description: The reading, in the essay syntax's Markdown.

The words quoted, verbatim from the official report or the enacted text, marking left-out words the Indigo Book way (R8.3; docs/style-guide.md): an ellipsis is three spaced periods, ". . .", never "..."; none at the start, where the first letter is capitalized in brackets ("[T]he"); " . . . ." with the sentence's own closing mark at the end of a sentence cut short; and none after a sentence that ends (checked by scripts/library/check_box_quotes.py and scripts/lint_records.py). Markdown.

pinpoint.description: Where the words are, as a citation's locator: "p. 561", "pp. 536-538", "¶ 58", "sec. 3". For a case, the page tells which opinion the words come from (site/src/lib/case-opinions.ts).

parenthetical.description: An Indigo Book parenthetical after the citation, without its parentheses, for words from a separate opinion: "White, J., concurring".

courtDays.description: Days in order, YYYY-MM-DD; several when the source names several, such as argument over three days.
